(Looks like I can click through to see number of deposits too, shame it's not in the table ;p) slots is better view imo https://beaconchain.withdrawal-devnet-7.ethpandaops.io/slots awesome as with block view you wouldn't see missed ones should be good for a while Hey, were you able to sync up your CL+ELs now? hey <@360491619402776577>, there was a spec change that constrained request sizes to 32 max. seems like this validation is currently missing from geth https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/commit/b7c5d3420e00648f456744d121ffbd929862924d Iiuc the min supported has to be 32 blocks and clients can choose their own max (which we don't) so yeah I guess we could add a max, but we don't need to ah, wording `error if the number of requested payload bodies is too large.` ... as determined by the implementation got it, ty yup, and i’m going to start some load testing on zhejiang later today although i don’t have a lot of validators rn i think pari can help just point some to the new builder Yea, lemme know when/how many and i can point them Yeah can totally help you pointing some to the builder Hi all, we've prepared a PR to introduce Builder API tests to hive over here: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/715 Kindly please take a look into the builder api parameters we've introduced for all Consensus clients, and let me know if there is any other parameter that could be worth to introduce in these tests. All tests are described here: https://github.com/ethereum/hive/pull/715/files#diff-86b0923201e6ac9e23e383128cd5a603ebf614cfeab94ff0d58d417d282acf1a Mentioning this here for more visibility: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/378 geth is using `withdrawal.address` but the spec says `withdrawal.recipient`. Discussion on the geth issue I opened seemed to indicate that `address` was preferred since it better matches whats in the EIP and CL layer, I've been out sick basically since posting that issue though so haven't had a chance to see what other ELs are returning in their e.g. `eth_getBlockByNumber` responses, but hoping we can settle on one or the other before Sepolia (ideally) or mainnet (worse case).
